new_statements.translation: 13. Musical tone [pitch] has mostly been noted. There occur: high ´, mid ¯, low `, as well as a falling tone ^. Rising tones were not observed. In what follows, however, no attempt has been made to take the tones into account in the grammatical analysis, since the material is not sufficient for this purpose.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Cibak is described as a tone language (three level tones high/mid/low plus a falling contour, no rising tone); the sketch makes no statement about word stress/dynamic accent, and even tone is only transcribed, not analysed, because the corpus (Lukas's 1952 notes from a single speaker) was too small.
new_statements.exceptions: none; author notes tone marks in the older sources (Meek etc.) are absent and that tones are ignored in the grammatical analysis
new_statements.domain_note: Transcription-level remark about the field notes (J. Lukas 1952, one speaker 'Wom', c. 25, Kwanda clan of the Cibak, bilingual in Kanuri); not a phonological analysis. Only section 13 and fragments of sections 1 and 6 were read (Google Books snippets); sections 7-12 of the Lautlehre were not seen in full, though volume-wide searches for Akzent/Betonung/Druck/Starkton with 'Cibak' returned nothing from this volume.
new_statements.identity_note: Hoffmann 1955 describes Cibak (self-name Cibik; also Chibbak/Chibbuk/Chibbok/Kibaku) = ciba1236, based chiefly on J. Lukas's 1952 field notes from one speaker (Wom, Kwanda clan, Cibak area, Margi District, Bornu Province) plus Meek 1931 and Letchworth material; same language as modern Kibaku of Chibok LGA. No dialect differentiation is made.
